name: dead leafless tree with gnarled bare branches and a thick trunk with exposed roots
label: wasteland_ruins/dead-tree

surfaces.part: moss/vine strip on left of trunk

answer.evidence: The trunk (rows 17-47) is a vertical column with a nearly constant width of 10-11 px. It flares at the base into roots in rows 43-47. It has no cap, no ellipse and no edge line with eave shadow. The branches are thin forked limbs drawn in flat side view. The moss on the left is a decor strip. For an organic dead tree this is a natural silhouette, but no horizontal top surface is drawn. The object is a front elevation, not a three-quarter view.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small, thin dead tree beside two full leafy trees. Its measured facts are acceptable: 8 visible tones per tile (tree-1a786c has 7, tree-d43edd has 29), 0% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels. The outline is a tinted dark brown beside the wood, not black. By eye, though, the trunk and branches read as only about 4 brown steps, with a thin dark edge, one lighter side and a mid fill. There are no bark grain clusters, no per-root shading, and no highlight dots, and the branches are one or two pixels wide and almost flat. The only extra detail is a small green moss strip on the trunk. Tree-d43edd has clumped leaves in many tones and shaded roots, and even the smaller tree-1a786c has varied clumps. Next to them the candidate looks thinner and more sticker-like. It needs more bark texture, more trunk and root shading steps, and more highlight variation to match the Beodeul bar.
